label: r4c1
name: half-roll, 1 epoch, lr 0.002
hypothesis: Same as r3c1 (1 PPO epoch), with lr going from 0.001 to 0.002. In r3c1, training success was only 0.09 at 25% of the run. A higher starting lr, which decays linearly, should shorten that slow start and leave more of the run for refinement. lr 0.002 was stable with 2 epochs (0.928). If dev success falls below about 0.91, or one seed collapses, 0.001 is better with 1 epoch.
last_analysis: Rolling the target by X/2 along x was the key fix: it took dev success from 0 to 0.59. After that, the best lever was trading PPO epochs for more fresh samples: 4 epochs gave 0.59, 2 gave 0.90 and 1 gave 0.9355, the current best. lr 0.002 with 2 epochs scored 0.928, about the same as lr 0.001 within noise. A deeper or wider trunk hurt both times (0.56 and 0.34), probably because its extra FLOPs cut the sample count. r3c1's training curve flattened at about 0.91 over the last quarter. The remaining failures are probably DONE timing and stacking order. This is the last round, so all three candidates keep r3c1's network and 1 PPO epoch and change one thing each: a higher learning rate, a longer return horizon so the +1 exact-build bonus gets more credit, and feeding global context back into each cell's features.
